name: Sean Duffy
role: U.S. Secretary of Transportation (since 2025); former Republican U.S. representative from Wisconsin (2011-2019)
summary: Duffy is a Republican from Wisconsin who as a House member opposed abortion and same-sex marriage, opposed the Affordable Care Act and gun restrictions, and backed tax cuts, a balanced budget amendment and fossil-fuel development. As Transportation Secretary under Trump he has cut climate, equity and DEI programs, cut funds to high-speed rail and offshore wind projects, tied grants to immigration cooperation and pushed deregulation of the auto and trucking industries. His public record on social issues beyond marriage and abortion, foreign policy and many economic questions is thin.

universal-healthcare.rationale: Campaigned against government-run health insurance, voted to repeal the ACA, and in 2018 called a single government plan 'kind of Soviet, kind of socialist'; his own plan relied on private coverage, HSAs and state high-risk pools.

markets-allocate-better.rationale: His health plan argued that more competition drives down prices and improves quality, and as secretary he framed DOT policy around cost-benefit analysis and deregulation; he did not state the principle in general terms.

tax-the-wealthy.rationale: Signed the Taxpayer Protection Pledge to oppose all tax increases and backed lower marginal rates and a flatter code.

regulate-corporations.rationale: Directed DOT to eliminate Biden-era rules and set up a deregulation task force and earlier proposed curbing the CFPB; his tougher oversight of Boeing was framed as safety enforcement rather than a general call for tighter corporate regulation.

surveillance-ok.rationale: Mixed record: voted in 2011 to extend PATRIOT Act roving wiretaps, but in 2013 he backed the USA FREEDOM Act ending bulk phone-record collection.

legalize-drugs.rationale: Received an F from NORML for his voting record on drug-law reform; no direct statement on legalization was found.

limit-guns.rationale: Said he would always defend the right to bear arms, opposed restricting gun purchase and possession, cosponsored national concealed-carry reciprocity, and in 2018 said an assault-weapons ban would hurt only law-abiding owners; he voted against universal background checks in 2019.

empower-police-military.rationale: His campaign platform called for fully funding troops, intelligence agencies and first responders; he did not call for expanded authority.

decide-locally.rationale: As secretary urged governors to take over NEPA review and signed a state-delegation agreement with Texas, and his health bill avoided pre-empting state malpractice law; but DOT also overrode New York's congestion pricing and conditioned grants on immigration cooperation.

same-sex-marriage.rationale: Stated in 2010 that marriage is one man and one woman, said he opposed government-sanctioned arrangements resembling marriage, and supported a federal marriage amendment; he accepted private contracts for inheritance and medical decisions. No later statement was found.

abortion-legal.rationale: Pledged to defend the right to life of the unborn, voted to bar federal funding of coverage that includes abortion, cosponsored a sex- and race-selection abortion ban, and backed a 20-week limit with a maternal-life exception.

correct-racial-injustice.rationale: His DOT directed elimination of programs promoting racial equity and removed equity requirements from grant programs, though he also said DOT should reach more communities with information about job opportunities.

empower-international-orgs.rationale: Cosponsored a 2013 resolution urging that the U.S. not sign the UN Arms Trade Treaty, citing risks to U.S. sovereignty and 'lawfare' through its tribunals.

free-trade.rationale: Told a 2018 town hall that tariffs could push other countries to lower trade barriers and leave industries better off, and as secretary advocated free trade in aerospace; he also backed steel and aluminum tariffs and proposed expanding presidential tariff authority.

open-borders.rationale: In 2018 said the border must be secured with a wall and technology and that e-verify is needed; as secretary tied DOT grants to cooperation with ICE.

limit-growth.rationale: Ordered all DOT policies and grants to rest on pro-economic-growth priorities and rescinded the highway greenhouse-gas measurement rule, describing climate policy as an 'agenda of control'.

drastic-climate-action.rationale: Voted to bar EPA from regulating greenhouse gases, signed the No Climate Tax Pledge, rescinded the DOT emissions-target rule, and his department called climate programs a 'Green New Scam'.

tax-inheritance.rationale: Voted for the Death Tax Repeal Act in 2015.

tariffs-protect-industry.rationale: Defended Trump's 2018 steel and aluminum tariffs as leverage against foreign barriers while acknowledging risk to Wisconsin cranberry growers; his stated aim was lower trade barriers rather than protection as such.

results-over-ideology.rationale: Signed a 2025 order that DOT actions rest on cost-benefit analysis and measurable benefits rather than ideological considerations.

school-vouchers.rationale: Voted to reauthorize the DC Opportunity Scholarship program and the SOAR Act, and a summary of the SOAR vote records the line that vouchers break the link between low income and low-quality schools.

avoid-deficit-stimulus.rationale: Ran against the 2009 stimulus, sponsored a bill applying remaining stimulus funds to the deficit, and proposed a balanced budget amendment.

work-for-welfare.rationale: Voted in 2013 to bar waivers of mandatory welfare work requirements.

expand-fossil-fuels.rationale: Voted to open the Outer Continental Shelf to drilling, backed offshore and eastern Gulf drilling in 2016, and as secretary approved a Texas deepwater oil port and LNG siting changes under an 'unleash American energy' agenda.

flat-income-tax.rationale: His 2010 platform said a flatter, fairer tax code would be ideal, while seeking lower marginal rates in the meantime.

space-expansion.rationale: As acting NASA administrator directed a lunar reactor, saying the U.S. is in a race with China to the moon and that a moon base is needed to go on to Mars.

end-racial-preferences.rationale: His department's 2025 rule removed race and sex presumptions from the DBE contracting program, with a statement that such preferences are unconstitutional; at his hearing he said hiring should be merit-based. The measure concerns contracting and federal hiring, not college admissions.

individual-pension-accounts.rationale: Wrote in 2010 that he had not and would not endorse privatizing Social Security.

gender-identity-recognition.rationale: His January 2025 memo directed DOT to eliminate programs and policies promoting 'gender identity policies'; no statement on legal recognition itself was found.

fiscal-rules-binding.rationale: Proposed a balanced budget amendment to the Constitution in 2011.

public-service-media.rationale: Voted against a 2011 bill to defund NPR, reportedly citing his constituents' use of public radio; he did not address editorial independence.

environment-over-liberty.rationale: At his hearing agreed that consumers should not be forced to buy cars Washington wants and that there is room for both electric and gas vehicles; his department later called EV mandates illegal.

notes: Many House-era answers rest on 2010 campaign-site statements and votes compiled by OnTheIssues; his positions since leaving Congress are mainly known through his actions as secretary, which are taken as his own only where his department stated them in his name. Same-sex marriage and abortion statements predate Obergefell and Dobbs and no later statement was found. Wikipedia and ENR descriptions of the DBE rule and funding actions are used only for the facts of what he did.
